method: Independent analytic derivation with numerical checks, separate from rendered labels
claims: A projected uniform circular motion x=A cos(omega t) has x second derivative = -omega squared x. Hooke restoring force -kx gives the same equation when omega squared=k/m. At x=0 acceleration is zero but velocity need not be.
Period 2pi/omega is independent of amplitude only in the ideal linear model; friction and nonlinear springs change the idealization.

checks.description: Numerical second derivative matches restoring acceleration
Endpoint speed zero, center speed maximum
Changing amplitude leaves the period unchanged

limitations: Numerical samples check implementations; general conclusions rest on the stated mathematical arguments.
